newsitem.title: PERU: Five hurt in oil ship blast off northern Peru.
newsitem.headline: Five hurt in oil ship blast off northern Peru.

text.p: A fuel tank exploded on an oil exploration ship off Peru's northern coast late Wednesday night, injuring five of the 20 people aboard, news and official sources said Thursday.
Local radio and the official news agency Andina said the Panama-registered ship was under contract to U.S.-based Petrotech, which operates an oil block off the northern Peruvian coast.

An official at Talara port, some 490 miles (785 kms) north of Lima, said authorities there received a call from distressed company officials about an explosion aboard the ship. But he could not confirm the number injured or provide other details of the incident.
"It was an urgent call. He (a company guard who went out to the ship) said two people were seen alive but he did not know anything else," the official said.
The explosion, when the ship was some 650 feet (200 meters) from the Tortugas pier, was reported at about 2230 local time Wednesday (0330 Thursday GMT), he added.
Further details were not immediately available.
